summary.text: Tarra Simmons is a Democratic member of the Washington House of Representatives, representing District 23-Position 1 since January 11, 2021, and is on the ballot for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
She is a civil rights attorney and a former registered nurse.

paragraphs.text: Simmons graduated from Central Kitsap High School in 1994, then earned an associate degree from Olympic College, a bachelor's degree from Pacific Lutheran University and a law degree from the Seattle University School of Law.

Her career experience includes working as executive director of the Civil Survival Project, as a Skadden Fellow with the Public Defender Association and as a legal intern with Columbia Legal Services.

In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, Simmons said she has personally experienced poverty, addiction and incarceration, and that she led an expansion of Washington's charity care law and helped restore voting rights to tens of thousands of Washingtonians.
She listed affordability, health care, behavioral health, housing, workers' rights and criminal justice reform as her areas of focus.
During the 2023-2024 session she was assigned to the Appropriations, Health Care and Wellness, and House Rules committees.
